commits.summary: example-targets runtime R2: the upstream build's dependency classpath filtered to the runtime scope (verification pending)
commits.body:
The first upstream-build job (20261114-170353, passed) recorded test-scope JARs, JUnit 5.14.4, opentest4j, apiguardian and commons-rng 1.7, as commons-numbers-core's runtime dependencies. runtime_upstream.py passed -Dmdep.includeScope=runtime to maven-dependency-plugin 3.9.0's build-classpath, but the plugin's descriptor (META-INF/maven/plugin.xml, from the JAR fetched from Maven Central and checked against its .sha1) reads that filter from ${includeScope}. Only the output file is ${mdep.outputFile}. The unknown property was ignored, and the listing was the test classpath. It now passes -DincludeScope=runtime, records the scope, and never passes the plugin's own options through from the recipe. The replay's result stood, since no class was shadowed, but the record misnamed the classpath.

Verified: the test's stand-in Maven now filters by scope as the plugin does, and its default dependencies include a test-scope JAR with the compile JAR's bytes. With the old property name, the ready preparation fails as shadowing; with the fix, test_runtime_upstream.py's 15 tests and the targets suite (111) pass. The real build is rerun as job 20261114-174017-example-targets-runtime-r2-the-upstream, expected to give each commit a classpath of the original, the adapter and the driver alone.

commits.summary: example-targets runtime R2: constructed mutants prepared on all three routes, their base patched with git apply, then built (verification pending)
commits.body:
A W1 mutant entry (a base revision, a patch by path and sha256, the mutation in words) was Unsupported in lock. Now it locks offline: the patch is rehashed against its recorded sha256, the files it modifies are read from it (modifications of existing text files only, hunk lines counted), and the base is locked by its own route. Its identity is mutant:<base>+<patch sha256>, with the scope constructed-mutation. Preparation applies the patch with git apply (checked first, each file's bytes recorded before and after, no enclosing repository consulted) and is never the base unpatched. The fixture route patches a copy of the base fixture, then runs the recipe. The upstream-build route patches the base commit's checkout and builds it, and the build must leave the checkout as patched. The published-artifact route checks out the base commit, compiles the patched Java files against the base's published JARs with the base classes' --release and debugging flags, and puts the classes in place of the base JAR's own in a copy of it. It refuses a signed JAR, release-specific copies of a patched class, a stale nested class and differing debug attributes, and it records an unpatched recompile to show the compiler's share of the difference.

Verified inline. Phase 0's own after-to-mutant patch (the sha256 build_fixtures.py records), applied by the fixture route, gives build_fixtures.py's mutant.jar byte for byte. On the published route the recompiled Gate.class is that JAR's own class. The mutation pair replays as the fixture's recorded controls on all three routes (the mutant fails at 65 on JDK 21 and 25). There are 11 lock refusals and the other blockers are tested. test_runtime.py has 63 tests and test_runtime_upstream.py 22. The integration script exits 0: contract 8 pass and 8 skip, targets suite 125, test_build 190, test_pipeline 29.

Job 20261114-180443-example-targets-runtime-r2-a-constructed runs the published route on real bytes. runtime_simplematch/mutation.json declares a mutant of spring-core 5.3.19 in W1's sidecar shape (beside target.json, since Phase 0's schema has no mutant). Its patch turns simpleMatch's suffix-branch endsWith into contains. The job expects the mutant to disagree with the Javadoc oracle at (*bc, bcx), (a*c*e, abced) and (*a*b, acba), and 5.3.19 nowhere. The earlier rerun 20261114-174017 passed: each commons-numbers classpath is exactly the original, the adapter and the driver, scope runtime. The brief's Progress records both, and its status is now waiting on that job.

commits.summary: example-targets runtime: the constructed-mutant job passed, R1-R5 and the acceptance done; VF-025's JARs needn't be in the history
commits.body:
Job 20261114-180443-example-targets-runtime-r2-a-constructed (at b5e28e26, collected as msotkvrv) passed. It ran the published-artifact route on real bytes: spring-core 5.3.19's PatternMatchUtils was recompiled from the v5.3.19 commit with suffix-anywhere.patch applied, using javac 25 with --release 8 -g -parameters read off the published class, into a copy of the JAR. On JDK 21 and 25, 5.3.19 agrees with the Javadoc oracle on all 45 probes, and the mutant disagrees at exactly the three predicted inputs. The unpatched recompile isn't byte-identical to the published class, and the record says so.

VF-025 (the job's three 1.4 MiB spring-core JARs exceed jj's snapshot limit): the runtime loop's decision is that they needn't be in the history. Two are re-acquired by sha256, and the mutant is rebuilt by runtime_slice.py --case simplematch-mutant, with its hashes in prepared.json. runtime_simplematch/README.md now records the job's result and this. Closing the finding needs the files ignored on main (.gitignore is shared), so it is left for the user or the coordinator.

The brief's Progress records the result and the acceptance evidence row by row, and its status is now done. What remains is for the merge, listed under Progress. Verified: test_runtime and test_runtime_upstream, 85 tests, pass.

commits.summary: example-targets reconcile: streams' traces recorded and logs copied; the merge blocked on an allow-list conflict only the user may resolve
commits.body:
Reconcile steps 1-3 of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md. All four streams finished done (runtime qrsyzzwu, negative zuoknpln, positive uzxpwmku, workflow nqztmpwy), and no stream or integration scope was active, nor any job pending. Each stream's last turns are recorded on its own branch (Record session traces: xvvuxmqs, mqnnxzkt, kxqozyus, svrtnrlo; negative's also carries the 8 allow-list proposals its last turn left uncommitted), and the 35 gitignored logs not yet in the default workspace were copied in. Those commits ran the workspaces' old sync.py, so their checks reported only the cross-workspace 'session ... has no manifest' errors that xyootzvm ends at the merge.

Step 4, the merge (jj new of the default line and the four branches, then sync.py regenerate), leaves exactly one conflict: llm-dlc/allowlist.json, where positive added 15 proposals and negative 8 to the same base of 23. Their union is 46 entries with no id differing between the sides, but this loop may not write that file, and taking one side with jj restore was refused as undermining oversight. So the merge was backed out uncommitted, and the brief's status is blocked on the user: resolve that one file in the merge, or allow the loop to.

Before backing out, example-targets-integration.sh ran on the merged tree: everything passes (targets suite 181, test_build.py 190, test_pipeline.py 29, every sidecar's plan, contract rows A0-A4, A6, A7) except contract A5. There all four fixture proof tasks are unresolved, because the claims name the parameter 'code' while the fixture's classes record no parameter names (arg0): VF-024's first point, reached now that the whole route runs. It waits for runtime's interface request to compile Phase 0's fixture recipe with -parameters, Phase 5 step 1's first item. The brief's reconcile step 4 doesn't anticipate a conflict in a file only a person may write; otherwise the brief is current.

commits.summary: example-targets reconcile steps 5-6: the four streams' Progress folded into the brief, their workspaces forgotten
commits.body:
Folds the runtime, negative, positive and workflow streams' Progress into llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md, as its reconcile step 5 asks. No stream had a timebox deferral. The one item deferred for the user, P1's and P3's upstream build route, was answered by decision 1's extension. Eleven groups of interface requests waited for the merge and are now Phase 5 step 1's ordered work list, grouped by file owner. They are: the fixture recipe's -parameters (contract A5's fix), the widened download hosts in runtime_maven.py (then P3), the six packets' mutants rewritten as W1 mutant revisions, the router regenerated for 285-300 and 305-307, readiness in the index, companion links, PreparedTarget's workdir and blocker fields, the result schema's existingTests for target receipts, a driver's invocation convention, smaller requests, and VF-025's .gitignore. Also recorded: the case packets' state at the merge (all source-locked, none prepared by a job), the runtime stream's five jobs, and the streams' for-review findings.

Each request was checked against the merged code: HOSTS still lists only Central and github.com, READINESS_IN_INDEX is False, build_fixtures.py has no JAVAC_FLAGS, examples/index.json has none of 285-307, all six packet sidecars declare their mutant as a controls entry, and result.schema.json still requires existingTests. sync.py check reports 0 errors at the merge, so the streams' cross-workspace 'has no manifest' errors are gone. Step 6 forgot the five workspaces (example-targets-runtime, -negative, -positive, -workflow, -integration); their directories under ../in-the-loop-example-targets-* are left for the user to delete. The brief's status is back to working.

commits.summary: example-targets Phase 5 step 1: the fixture recipe compiles with -parameters, so contract A5 passes
commits.body:
Phase 0's fixture recipe (examples/tools/targets/fixtures/build_fixtures.py) compiled the Gate classes without parameter names, so the verifier called the claims' `code` arg0, and every fixture proof task of contract A5 came back unresolved on the merged streams (VF-024's first point). The recipe now has JAVAC_FLAGS = ("-parameters",), which runtime's fixture route already read, and records the flags in its manifest. Runtime's toolchain record lists the recipe's flags too. make_records.py remade records/: every fixture JAR's sha256 changed, but the controls' outputs, the oracle's verdicts on JDK 21 and 25, and the gap scan's three regex calls did not.

Three runtime tests pinned the old bytes and were updated: the verifier's scope names `code` from MethodParameters, the flags test builds its no-names variant with the flags removed and now checks that variant's arg0 scope, and the published mutant route's recompile carries -parameters from its base classes and still gives build_fixtures.py's mutant bytes. runtime_calibrate.py's docstring and the fixtures README are updated; the README also lists claims/.

commits.summary: example-targets Phase 5 step 1: the download hosts widened to repo.spring.io and services/plugins.gradle.org; P3's build plugin needs credentials
commits.body:
runtime_maven.HOSTS now holds decision 1's extended hosts: Maven Central, github.com, repo.spring.io, services.gradle.org and plugins.gradle.org. A new test, which failed first, checks that they are allowed and that the rest stays refused: other hosts and look-alikes, the Gradle CDNs as hosts or redirects, http, a user name or port, and a SNAPSHOT on repo.spring.io. Refusal messages name the five hosts.

The Gradle route itself was not built. HEAD requests showed that P3's (307) buildscript plugin, spring-build-conventions 0.0.23.RELEASE, is on no anonymous repository: repo.spring.io answers 401, and plugins.gradle.org redirects to Maven Central, which has 404. Its upstream build would stop at the buildscript, so it was not queued. Runtime's Gradle blocker now says that the route is missing, not that the policy forbids it; a distribution on another host is still outside the policy (new test). 307's sidecar blocker, handoff, notes and README record this and name the narrower slice (each commit's BCrypt.java compiled alone) as the alternative. Whether to use repo.spring.io credentials or that slice is left for review. 305's wording about decision 1 is updated.

Brief out of date: Progress's request 2 said 'Runtime's Gradle toolchain blocker goes with it. Then P3 (307) by its pinned upstream build, as a job'; neither happened, for the reason above. Decision 1's extension also assumed that P3's build becomes possible, which it doesn't without credentials.

commits.summary: example-targets Phase 5 step 1: the six packets' mutation controls become W1 mutant revisions, with tasks of their own
commits.body: Each deep packet (285, 286, 287, 305, 306, 307) declared its constructed mutant only as a controls entry of kind mutation on its base revision, which no task prepared. Each patch is now workflow W1's revision mutant (base fixed-release, after or release-after; the patch's sha256 unchanged; the mutation described in words), the after of a new mutation pair. Each packet gains a mutant-replay task (the concrete controls on that pair: base holds, mutant fails) and a claim task expected refuted: mutant-security, fixed-security's claim on the mutant (285-287), or mutant-preservation, preservation's claim over the mutation pair (305-307; 306's is gate A4's nearby mutation). The mutation control now names the revision mutant, as the fixture's does. Side effect: the patch is no longer among fixed-security's or replay's controls, so those plans' input keys changed (and replay's claim key for 305-307); no packet has a receipt, so nothing went stale. Runtime's slice runtime_simplematch/mutation.json moved into its target.json unchanged, and runtime_slice.py no longer merges it. The READMEs, example.json notes and the slice README say so.

commits.summary: example-targets Phase 5 step 1: the router regenerated, so index.json and examples/README.md list 285-300 and 305-307
commits.body:
Request 4 of the merge's interface requests (llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md, Progress). The streams couldn't write the coordinator's generated files, so examples/index.json and examples/README.md had none of the 19 new folders, and find.py couldn't reach the catalog or the positive packets. A new test, examples/tools/targets/test_packets.py's RouterTest, failed for those 19 folders. It checks that the committed router lists every numbered folder and gives each sidecar example a target projection. python3 examples/tools/build.py --index-only regenerated both files. The 19 folders gained rows, tag links and index entries. Example 105's entry gained its migration notes and its target projection (role calibration), and its historical verdictLabel is unchanged. No other entry changed.

Verified: llm-dlc/tools/example-targets-integration.sh exits 0 (contract 16, targets suite 188, test_build.py 190, test_pipeline.py 29, build.py --plan). find.py --family spring-data-binding finds 286, 288, 299 and 306, and --role positive finds 305-307. --readiness still matches nothing until request 5 sets READINESS_IN_INDEX. Two tag issues are noted for request 6. The external-target tag misses 105 and 305-307. Example 306's request-binding tag describes handler parameters, so data-binding fits better.
